posts.title: JXL CBZ Archive For Manga Downloader
posts.content:
Currently, AnymeX is developing a downloader for manga. To optimize storage space without sacrificing image quality, I suggest adding support for **JXL (JPEG XL)** as an internal image format within **CBZ** archives.

### Why JXL?
1. **Superior Compression:** JXL typically offers **20-30% better compression** than WebP and significantly better results than traditional JPEG/PNG.
2. **Lossless Transcoding:** JXL allows for lossless transcoding of existing JPEGs, meaning we can reduce file sizes without any generation loss.
3. **Future-Proofing:** High-end manga readers like **Mihon** and **TachiyomiJ2K** already support JXL in CBZ. Adding this would make AnymeX downloads compatible with the most efficient storage standards in the manga community.

### Implementation Suggestions for Flutter:
Since Flutter doesn't natively decode JXL, the following packages/libraries can be used to handle the heavy lifting:
- **jxl_coder (Plugin):** A Flutter wrapper for the JXL decoding/encoding library (available on pub.dev).
- **libjxl via FFI:** Directly bundling the C++ reference implementation for maximum performance.

### Proposed Workflow:
1. **Downloader:** Add a toggle in Settings: "Use JXL Compression for Downloads."
2. **Conversion:** During the download process, convert fetched images to `.jxl` before wrapping them into a `.cbz` (ZIP) container.
3. **Reader:** Integrate a JXL decoder into the manga viewer to ensure seamless rendering of these high-efficiency files.

Implementing this would give AnymeX a significant edge in storage management, especially for users with large offline libraries.

3. **Future-Proofing:** High-end manga readers like **Mihon** and **TachiyomiJ2K** already support JXL in CBZ. Adding this would make AnymeX downloads compatible with the most efficient storage standards in the manga community.

### Implementation Suggestions for Flutter:
Since Flutter doesn't natively decode JXL, the following packages/libraries can be used to handle the heavy lifting:
- **jxl_coder (Plugin):** A Flutter wrapper for the JXL decoding/encoding library (available on pub.dev).
- **libjxl via FFI:** Directly bundling the C++ reference implementation for maximum performance.

### Proposed Workflow:
1. **Downloader:** Add a toggle in Settings: "Use JXL Compression for Downloads."
2. **Conversion:** During the download process, convert fetched images to `.jxl` before wrapping them into a `.cbz` (ZIP) container.
3. **Reader:** Integrate a JXL decoder into the manga viewer to ensure seamless rendering of these high-efficiency files.

posts.title: Long Press for Vertical Speed Selection (Floating UI)
posts.content:
Enable a **long press anywhere on the video** to trigger a **vertical floating speed selector**. As the user moves their finger **up or down**, it adjusts the playback speed. Releasing the finger resets speed back to normal (1x).

### 🔧 How It Works:

1. **Long Press to Activate**:
   * Holding anywhere on the screen for \~0.5 sec brings up a **floating speed UI** next to the finger.
   * The UI shows multiple speed levels (e.g., 0.25x → 3x), like a vertical slider or labels.

2. **Move Finger Up/Down to Set Speed**:
   * Moving **up = faster**, moving **down = slower**.
   * Real-time preview: the video plays at the selected speed while sliding.
   * A tooltip follows the finger showing the current speed (e.g., `2.0x`).

3. **Release to Reset**:
   * Once the finger is lifted, **playback speed instantly returns to 1x**.
   * The floating UI disappears.

### 💡 Why It’s Awesome:
* Super quick speed adjustment with **no UI clutter**.
* Perfect for **temporary fast-forward or slow-mo** moments.
* Feels natural and fluid — like **touch-based jog control**.
* Doesn’t interrupt playback, doesn’t need multiple taps.

[This is an example of how it looks like](https://screenapp.io/app/#/shared/mNSmo5_aNF)

posts.content:
**Constraint 1:**
The app must support up to 5 fully isolated user profiles. Each profile is a completely independent environment — its own linked accounts, settings, preferences, and history. No data is shared between profiles.

**Constraint 2:**
On first launch, the app must display a mandatory Profile Creation screen. The user must create at least one profile before accessing the app. This screen cannot be skipped.

**Constraint 3:**
Each profile must store: a user-defined name, avatar , creation date, last used timestamp, and badges showing which services are linked (AniList, MAL, etc.).

**2. Profile Startup Behavior**

**Constraint 1:**
If only one profile exists, the app must skip all profile selection screens and boot directly into that profile.

**Constraint 2:**
If two or more profiles exist, the app must display a Profile Selection screen at startup showing all profiles as selectable cards.

**Constraint 3:**
The Profile Selection screen must include a checkbox option: *"Open this profile automatically next time."* If checked when selecting a profile, the app skips the selection screen on future launches and opens that profile directly.

**Constraint 4:**
The auto-start preference must be resettable from Settings, which re-enables the Profile Selection screen.

**3. Profile Switching**

**Constraint 1:**
The user must be able to switch profiles mid-session by long-pressing their avatar/profile icon anywhere it appears in the app.

**Constraint 2:**
Long-pressing the avatar must show a profile switcher overlay listing all profiles. The currently active profile must be visually marked and cannot be re-selected.

posts.title: Extension Home Page – Library Based
posts.content:
Make the Extension Home Page fully powered by the shared Library instead of acting like a simple content browser.

Since all services (AniList, MAL, SIMKL, Extension) share one unified Library, the Extension home should also use the Library as its primary data source  just like API clients use synced list data.

🔹 Core Idea
* When a user opens the Extension tab:
* It should display sections generated from the Library
* Default lists + Custom lists should appear as optional home sections
* All media types (Anime, Manga, Novels, Movies, Shows) should follow the same categorization used in Library tabs
* This keeps consistency across services while making Extension feel fully integrated.

🔹 How It Would Work
* Library becomes the primary source for Extension Home.
* Sections like Watching, Planning, Completed, Custom Lists can be toggled on/off.
* Media type tabs (Anime / Manga / Movies / Shows / Novels) should filter all home sections dynamically.
* The layout customization system should work similar to API clients.

🔹 Why This Is Important
* Keeps experience consistent across all 4 services.
* Makes Extension feel like a first-class service, not separate.
* Reduces duplication of logic.
* Strengthens the unified Library concept.
* Gives users a familiar and customizable home layout.

   - This feature applies **only to items not added** to the user’s list.

   - **Synopsis**:  
     - Display the synopsis.  
     - If the synopsis is too long, include an **expand/collapse button** (e.g., "Read More" / "Show Less").  
   - **Synonyms**: Display alternate titles.  
   - **Genres**: List the genres associated with the anime/manga.  
   - **Tags**: Show related tags to provide more context.  

4. **Dismissal**:  
   - The popup can be dismissed by:  
     - Tapping outside the popup.  
     - Clicking a visible **close button**.

posts.title: Local Source (Bring Your Own Content)
posts.content:
**Enhancing AnyMex Library: Local Source Support for Anime & Manga**

With AnyMex already featuring a library, it’s time to take it to the next level by introducing **Local Source Support**—allowing users to bring their own content. Similar to Aniyomi’s local source feature, this functionality will enable users to manually add anime and manga to their library by placing files in a designated directory.

## **Local Anime Source**
For users who prefer to download and organize their anime, AnyMex will support adding locally stored anime episodes.

### **How It Works**
1. Inside the designated storage location (e.g., `/AnyMex/`), a `localanime` folder will be created.
2. Users can add anime series as separate folders inside `/AnyMex/localanime/`.
3. Episodes in **.mp4** and **.mkv** formats should be placed inside the respective series folder.
4. A `.nomedia` file can be added to prevent images and videos from appearing in the device’s gallery.
5. Users can access their local anime via **Browse → Sources → Local Anime Source**.
6. If new episodes are added, a manual refresh (pulling down the episode list) is required.

### **Folder Structure Example**
```
/AnyMex/localanime/
   ├── [Anime Title]/
   │    ├── cover.jpg
   │    ├── ep01.mp4
   │    ├── ep02.mkv
```

messages.content:
## **Local Manga Source**
For users who prefer managing their own manga collection, AnyMex will support locally stored manga files.

### **How It Works**
1. Inside the designated storage location (e.g., `/AnyMex/`), a `local` folder will be created.
2. Users can add manga series as separate folders inside `/AnyMex/local/`.
3. Each manga chapter should be placed inside a separate folder containing images in **.jpg**, **.png**, etc., or as an archive file (**ZIP/CBZ, RAR/CBR, EPUB**).
4. A `.nomedia` file can be added to prevent images from appearing in the device’s gallery.
5. Users can access their local manga via **Browse → Sources → Local Source**.
6. If new chapters are added, a manual refresh (pulling down the chapter list) is required.

### **Folder Structure Example**
```
/AnyMex/local/
   ├── [Manga Title]/
   │    ├── cover.jpg
   │    ├── [Chapter 1]/
   │    │    ├── page_1.jpg
   │    │    ├── page_n.jpg
   │    ├── [Chapter 2].cbz
```

## **Archive File Support**
- ZIP/CBZ archives are supported, but internal folder structures will be ignored.
- The archive should be placed directly inside the **Series Folder**.
- All images inside the archive will be treated as part of a single chapter.

### **Archive Structure Example**
```
/AnyMex/local/
   ├── [Manga Title]/
   │    ├── cover.jpg
   │    ├── [Chapter 1].zip
   │    │    ├── image_1.jpg
   │    │    ├── image_n.jpg
```

With these additions, AnyMex will provide a **seamless offline experience**, allowing users to not only download content through the app but also integrate their manually collected anime and manga into the library effortlessly.

posts.title: Allow adding custom (empty) items to library
posts.content:
Add an option to create custom/empty items in the library for all content types (Anime, Manga, Novels, AnymeX shows).

On each library tab, include a setting or button like “Add Custom Item”.

When creating a custom item, the user should be able to:
- Upload or set a poster/image
- Enter a title/name
- Select the content type (Anime / Manga / Novel / etc.)

Once created:
- Items should be stored and tracked locally (not tied to AniList, MAL, SIMKL, etc.)
- Users can add unlimited custom items
- It should behave like a normal item for tracking progress

Behavior:
- Extension selector works based on the selected type (same as normal items)
- Only one tab:
  - Watch / Read
- No Details or Comments tabs (not needed for custom items)

Why this is useful:

Many anime, manga, or novels are not available on tracking services.

Currently, users have to:
- Pick a random/incorrect title
- Use it just to access extensions and track progress

This causes:
- Wrong tracking data
- Confusing libraries
- Poor experience

With this feature:
- Users can track anything they want properly
- No need to depend on external databases
- Cleaner and more flexible library system

Summary:
Custom local items will make the library more flexible, accurate, and user-friendly by allowing tracking of content that isn’t officially listed anywhere.
